title: Amazon Aurora
description: Understand Amazon Aurora architecture, Aurora MySQL and PostgreSQL compatibility, serverless mode, global databases, and replicas.

data.text: Amazon Aurora is AWS's cloud-native relational database built for the cloud. It is compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL, but it uses a distributed storage architecture that makes it faster, more available, and more durable than standard RDS.

Aurora separates compute from storage. The database engine runs on Aurora Replicas (compute instances), while the data lives on a distributed, self-healing storage volume that automatically replicates six copies across three Availability Zones.

data.title: Key Architectural Differences from Standard RDS
items: Storage automatically grows in 10 GB increments up to 128 TB
Data is replicated 6 ways across 3 AZs — standard RDS only does 2 copies

data.text: Aurora Serverless automatically starts up, shuts down, and scales capacity based on your application's needs. You pay per second for only the capacity you use. It is ideal for infrequently used applications, development environments, and variable workloads.

Aurora Global Database lets you replicate your database across multiple AWS Regions with a typical replication lag of less than 1 second. It is designed for globally distributed applications that need disaster recovery and low-latency local reads.

data.title: Aurora vs RDS Cost
data.text: Aurora is usually more expensive than standard RDS. However, its performance, durability, and reduced downtime often make it the better choice for production workloads.

Aurora supports up to 15 low-latency read replicas. Because Aurora replicas share the same storage volume, replication lag is almost zero. You can also have cross-region read replicas for disaster recovery and global reads.

terms.definition: A compute instance that shares the same underlying storage as the primary, providing fast read scaling with near-zero replication lag.
A configuration where Aurora automatically adjusts capacity up and down based on application demand.
A single Aurora database that spans multiple AWS Regions with fast replication for disaster recovery.
The endpoint that routes all write traffic to the current primary instance in an Aurora cluster.

data.title: Create an Aurora Serverless Cluster
data.description: Create an Aurora Serverless v2 MySQL cluster in the AWS console and explore how capacity scaling works.
steps: Open the RDS console and click 'Create database'
Select Aurora MySQL or Aurora PostgreSQL
Set minimum and maximum Aurora Capacity Units (ACUs)
Create the cluster and monitor the 'Capacity' metric in CloudWatch
data.expectedOutcome: You will see how Aurora Serverless scales automatically. Try running a heavy query and watch the capacity increase.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Aurora separates compute from storage for better performance and durability
Aurora Serverless automatically scales capacity and is billed per second
Aurora Global Database enables cross-region replication with sub-second lag
Aurora is generally faster and more available than standard RDS
data.takeaway: Aurora is AWS's premium relational database offering. Choose it when you need high performance, high availability, and automatic scaling.
